section: The values and principles of the UK
explanation: Democracy means government by the people through elected representatives, and is a fundamental principle of British life.

angles.q: In a democracy, who ultimately chooses the government?
alts: Under a democratic system, government is chosen by whom?
Democracy places the choice of government in whose hands?

tf.s: In the UK, the government is chosen by the people through elections.
British values include respect for democratic institutions.

section: The values and principles of the UK
explanation: Individual liberty means people are free to make their own choices, within the limits set by the law.

angles.q: Individual liberty in the UK is limited by what?
alts: Personal freedom in the UK operates within which limits?

tf.s: People in the UK are free to make their own choices within the law.

section: The values and principles of the UK
explanation: Tolerance of those with different faiths and beliefs is a fundamental principle. The UK does not tolerate extremism.

angles.q: British values require tolerance towards people with different what?
alts: Tolerance in the UK is expected towards those with different what?

tf.s: The UK welcomes those who are willing to share its values.
Intolerance towards other faiths is acceptable in the UK.

section: The values and principles of the UK
explanation: Residents are expected to respect the law, respect the rights of others, treat people fairly, look after themselves and their family, and care for their area and the environment.

angles.q: Which of these is expected of everyone living in the UK?
alts: Which responsibility do UK residents share?

tf.s: Residents should respect the right of others to hold their own opinions.
Looking after your family is one of the responsibilities listed in the handbook.
UK residents may choose which laws to obey.

section: The values and principles of the UK
explanation: Rights shared by everyone in the UK include freedom of belief, freedom of speech, freedom from unfair discrimination, a fair trial and a vote.

angles.q: Which of these is a right shared by everyone in the UK?
alts: Everyone resident in the UK shares which of these rights?

tf.s: People in the UK are free to change their religion.
Freedom from unfair discrimination is a right in the UK.

explanation: Applicants for settlement or citizenship must show English language ability and knowledge of life in the UK, then attend a citizenship ceremony.

angles.q: Where is a citizenship ceremony usually held?
alts: Citizenship ceremonies normally take place where?

angles.q: To whom is the oath of allegiance made?
angles.a: The monarch and their heirs and successors
alts: New citizens swear allegiance to whom?

tf.s: Those who prefer not to swear by God may make a solemn affirmation.
New citizens receive a certificate of British citizenship.

section: Taking the Life in the UK Test
explanation: The Life in the UK Test is taken in English at a registered test centre, though it can be taken in Welsh or Scottish Gaelic by arrangement.

angles.q: Besides English, in which languages can the Life in the UK Test be taken?
alts: The test may be taken in which other languages by arrangement?

tf.s: The Life in the UK Test must be booked in advance.
All test questions come from the official handbook.

explanation: The UK is the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland. Great Britain is England, Scotland and Wales.

angles.q: Which country is part of Great Britain but not a separate island?
alts: Which of these countries shares the island of Great Britain with England and Scotland?

tf.s: The UK is governed by the Parliament at Westminster.
Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland also have devolved administrations.

explanation: The pound sterling is the UK currency. Scotland and Northern Ireland issue their own banknotes, valid throughout the UK.

angles.q: Banknotes issued in Scotland are valid where?
alts: Where can Scottish banknotes legally be used?

explanation: Welsh is spoken in Wales, Gaelic in parts of Scotland, and Irish Gaelic and Ulster Scots in Northern Ireland.

angles.q: Which language is taught in schools throughout Wales?
alts: Alongside English, which language do Welsh schools teach?

explanation: Crown dependencies such as Jersey and the Isle of Man are self-governing and linked to the Crown, but are not part of the UK.

angles.q: Crown dependencies are linked to what?
alts: Jersey and the Isle of Man are closely linked to what?
